title: I wanted to stop blowing funded accounts
author: br-hm
selftext:
So over the past few years I've blown a few funded accounts over the years. Every time I kept changing strategies, re-optimizing, etc. Same results every time.

I never really looked at how an individual strategy fits in a portfolio. I started wondering if maybe I should treat my forex portfolio the same as any other trading portfolio, where I put more/less risk in a strategy depending on it's individual performance. 

So I built an optimizer that splits the risk between strategies based on how they've actually performed together, instead of me guessing. Here's the same 5 strategies on a $100k account with a $10k drawdown limit, Jan 2020 to Apr 2026:

https://i.redd.it/acla81k7no2i1.png

Equal 0.5% risk on each: net profit $335k, max drawdown $20.3k, return factor 16.51. That's double the limit, so the account would have been gone.

Optimized allocation: net profit $237k, max drawdown $9,995, return factor 23.75.

So yeah, the equal risk version makes way more money on paper. It's also the one that blows the account. That's basically what kept happening to me. I was looking at the profit number and ignoring the drawdown.

Obviously this is a backtest, and the allocation was fitted on the same data, so don't read it as a promise of anything. The optimizer does run a monte carlo with possible combinations and does an IS/OOS split.

The other thing that used to drive me nuts is not knowing whether a drawdown is normal. Every losing streak I'd wonder if the strategy was broken or just having a bad month, and I'd either turn off something that was fine or keep running something that had stopped working. So I made a second tool that compares each live strategy to its own backtest and shows whether it's inside the range you'd expect. In the second screenshot, XAUUSD is tracking fine and GBPUSD is flagged as running below its usual range. That's the call I used to make on gut feel.

https://i.redd.it/nqu5b2ipno2i1.png

Happy to answer questions about how it works. The dashboard is on [cephic.io](http://cephic.io) and it has demo data so no sign-up is needed if you simply wanna give it a look.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the fitted-on-the-same-data part is the one I'd lean on. weights chosen to keep max drawdown under 10k on 2020-2026 will land at 9,995 almost by construction, so that drawdown is the one number the optimizer can't give you honestly. the check I'd run is fitting on 2020-2023 alone and seeing if those weights still hold the limit on 2024-26, since strategies that look uncorrelated tend to lose together in the bad months.

replies.author: br-hm
replies.body: The chosen allocation is from IS/OOS splits. Also, it’s more to see whether a strategy is even worth adding to the portfolio, and adjusting allocation according to correlation, rather than worst case scenario or guesswork
